Title: Corporate Firewall Setup and Whitelisting Marvelous Designer Endpoints
Content: Applicable for: Enterprise users who are using corporate firewall and whitelisting policies First, make sure you have corporate firewalls and whitelisting policies in place on your network systems. Please contact your company's IT or security team for this whitelisting and firewall setup. Note Marvelous Designer authentication servers only allow HTTPS communication. Therefore, only port 443 is discussed in this article. Until Marvelous Designer 10 version, the verify: peer option inside the Marvelous Designer 10 software was disabled, but from Marvelous Designer 11 version it is enabled and built and distributed. So if your company uses SSL Inspection on your secure network system, please check its detailed settings. If you need to whitelist Marvelous Designer authentication servers for Marvelous Designer logins on a secure network, add the information below to your security solution. If you are experiencing problems downloading in-app assets, please add the domain*.clo-set.com to your whitelist. Non-firewalled customers may not need whitelisting of Marvelous Designer authentication servers. If you need whitelisting and use a corporate firewall IPs to be whitelisted 52.1.24.50 52.20.29.14 Domains to be whitelisted sapi.clo3d.com sapi.clo3d-china.com *.clo-set.com Protocol and port to whitelisted https (443 port) Enable the Firewall option in Marvelous Designer login window (see the screenshot at the bottom) If you need whitelisting but don't use a corporate firewall IPs to be whitelisted 52.1.24.50 52.20.29.14 Domains to be whitelisted api.clo3d.com api.clo3d-china.com *.clo-set.com Protocol and port to whitelisted https (443 port) Disable the Firewall option in Marvelous Designer login window (see below figure) Firewall option at Marvelous Designer login screen Note that the information provided below is only for customers using enterprise firewall solutions, not Windows or macOS firewall features. Check with your company's IT or security team whether you use a firewall.

Title: Avatar Properties (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Set the avatar's properties. When you select an avatar, its properties appear in the property window. Avatar Properties Properties Description Information Name Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. Model You can change the type of avatar. Surface Skin Offset Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. Static Friction The friction when a garment is in stationary position. Kinetic Friction The friction when a garment is moving. Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0) Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. Note: When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. Soft Body Stiffness Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. Material (Selected) Set the Material of the avatar. Miscellaneous Mesh Type Indicates the type of avatar mesh. Element Count Indicates the number of points in the mesh. Smooth Avatar Smooth Toggles the Smooth option on or off. If the option is on, the mesh on the avatar's surface will be divided as set in 'Division Level'. Division Level Can be split by a factor of 1 to 5. Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0)

Title: Auto Convert to Avatar (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Auto Convert to Avatar (ver. 2024.0) Automatically converts externally created avatars into default avatar types in Marvelous Designer. Automatically convert your custom avatar into a compatible avatar of matching default internal skeleton and motions. Steps Run it along the path below. Location Main menu Avatar Auto Convert to Avatar Please refer to the table below and automatically convert it into the avatar of Marvelous Designer. Basic Original File - Import the desired avatar file format (OBJ, AVT, FBX only). NOTE: This tool is recommended to be used with Human shaped Avatar Mesh in an A-pose. Gender - You can select the option of the desired gender. - The format is as follows: Female Male Girl (7-20) Boy (7-20) Kid (2-6) Baby (6-18m) Converting option Automatic Automatically converts the avatar's body shape. Custom (Maintain current rig) The body shape is converted while maintaining the joint positions of the original avatar file. Exclude hands and feet: When the "Exclude Hands and Feet option" is selected, the Marvelous Designer avatar's hands and feet will be retained when transforming the avatar's body shape. Converted Type MD Skin Style Keep the body shape of the original avatar file and convert only the appearance to a Marvelous Designer Avatar and add joint points. Rigging Only Maintains the body shape and appearance of the original avatar file, only adding articulation points. Size Editable Change the default avatar body shape and add articulation points in the Marvelous Designer to allow for size editing while preserving the shape of the file to be converted. Save Path File Name(AVT) Name the avatar you want to save as an AVT file. File path Specify the path of the file you want to save. End Result The Avatars will appear in the 3D window based on the selected options chosen.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Internal Damping
Content: Objective Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. Note: Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference. Therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Internal Damping

Title: Software Remote Logout
Content: Problems Worked with Marvelous Designer on the office computer and tried to log in to Marvelous Designer with a home computer, but it says it is already in use. Tried to log in to Marvelous Designer on a new computer, but it says another computer is already in use. Worked on the desktop and tried to log in to the laptop, but it says it is already in use. How to log out 1) Log in to the Marvelous Designer website and go to My account. https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage 2) Check the Account tab. 3) Click the "LOGOUT" button next to the software remote logout. Read more When the Marvelous Designer software is running, the Logout button does not appear on the Marvelous Designer website. After the Marvelous Designer software has completely quit, the Logout button is displayed on the Marvelous Designer website. If you exit by selecting "Log out" or "Deactivation" in the software, the Logout button will not appear on the Marvelous Designer website. Depending on the region, network, and Marvelous Designer server status, the Logout button may be delayed up to 15 minutes. Logout does not cancel your Marvelous Designer license or subscription.

Title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
Content: OBJ Import/Export Objective An OBJ file is used when saving Scene and Props that organize Avatar and surrounding environment. If the OBJ type is an Avatar, the OBJ file is able to wear Garments but if it is a Trim, the Garment passes through it as it does not recognize it as an object. For detailed instruction on how to use OBJ files as Trims, refer to Load As Trim. Furthermore, OBJ files with the same Mesh structure (net-shaped structure expresses 3D objects) is able to be "Morphed" to change Avatar's appearance. Morphing refers to slowly changing the appearance of one object into another, and this function can be used to change Avatar's poses or body type. This function is useful when changing Poses of an Avatar in Garments. For detailed instruction, refer to Load as Morph Target. Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in *.obj file and they are compatible with other 3D software. When exporting Garments in an *.obj file, a *.mtl file is also created, and this *.mtl file saves material information of the Garment. Location OBJ Import Main Menu File Import OBJ Additional OBJ Import Main Menu File Import (Add) OBJ OBJ Export Main Menu File Export OBJ Selected OBJ Export Main Menu File Export OBJ (Selected) Operation OBJ Import Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Select a file and click OK. Import OBJ window appears. Set details and click OK. Note: OBJ Import Detail Settings Object Type Load as Avatar Imports an object as an avatar and replaces it with the original avatar. Add Arrangement Points &ampBVs: Turn on this option to generate Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points fit to the imported OBJ (ver4.2.0). Note: This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. "Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose." Load as Trim Due to nonfunctional collision detection, objects pass through garments (ver3.0.0). Load as Garment Import an object as a 3D Garment. Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map: Toggle on this option to generate Patterns based on UV Map information (ver4.2.0). Load as Morph Target Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Scale Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of an object. When the OBJ is placed below the ground, please toggle on Align Bottom to Ground option to pull up the OBJ file above the ground (ver4.2.0). Note: Load as Garment - Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map OBJ Additional Import Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import (Add) OBJ The Add File window appears. Set details and click OK. OBJ Export Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Export OBJ (Selected) Save File window appears. Select desired location to store, and click Save. Export OBJ window appears. Set details and click OK. Note: OBJ Export Detail Settings Object Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Note: If OBJ(Selected) is utilized, selected Patterns are being checked in the 3D and 2D window. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Single Object Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects Exports selected object as multiple objects. Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. Note: Thickness is available to be exported when pattern's mesh is Quad (ver2.3.0). Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. Image File Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: File Name_0, File Name_1. Texture Size Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Include Internal Shape: Includes internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Axis Conversion Changes directions of object's each axis. File Save with Texture File (*.zip): Exports .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting (ver4.2.0). Exclude Ambient Map &amp Color (Modo): Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Alpha Map: Alpha Map is included when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Meta Data (*.xml) : Exports garment's pattern(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude Ambient color value when saving materials. Note: OBJ Export Updates Internal Line(s)/Shape(s) export (including FBX). Thickness export for Quad Mesh. Front, side and back meshes separate export. Load as Garment Objective Import and simulate OBJ files from other 3D software programs (Maya, 3DS MAX and etc). Location Main Menu File Import (Add) OBJ to Garment Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import (Add) OBJ to Garment Open File window appears. Select a file and click OK. OBJ to Garment window appears. Set details and click OK. Load as Morph Target Objective Morph uses two different OBJ files to slowly change object's appearance. Marvelous Designer's default avatars can be modified at Change Avatar Size menu or posed with Show X-Ray Joints function, other 3D software may not have basic Joints set for designed objects, parts may be lost when creating a compatible COLLADA file. As such, this menu can be used to change the object's body type. At least two *.obj files with the same Mesh structure are needed to morph the object. Use this menu to import objects from different 3D software as Avatars, and dress them or change their Poses. Location Import OBJ Main Menu File Import OBJ Open Morph Target OBJ Import Options Window Object Type Load as Morph Target Operation Choose two *.obj files to morph. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Select the first file to import and click OK. Import OBJ window appears. Set details and click OK. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Select the second file to import and click OK. Open Morph Target window appears. Follow the indicated guideline: OBJ Import Options Window Object Type Load as Morph Target Set details and click OK. Note: File name with #(special character) is not going to be loaded. Load as Trim Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to organize Trims as well as the Avatars in Garments. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it, however when the same file is loaded as Trims, the Garment does not register it as an object therefore it passes through it. Location OBJ Import Main Menu File Import OBJ Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window Object Type Load as Trim Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Choose file to import and click OK. Import OBJ window appears. Select Load as Trim in Object Type. Set details and click OK. Load as Avatar Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to use as Avatars in Marvelous Designer. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it. Location OBJ Import Main Menu File Import OBJ Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window Object Type Load as Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu File Import OBJ Open File window appears. Choose file to import and click OK. Import OBJ window appears. Select Load as Avatar in Object Type. Set details and click OK.

Title: Account Manual
Content: Company ID - End User ID Relationship diagram Difference between End User and Company ID Company ID: Your "Company ID" is an administrator account that can manage "End User IDs" owned by the license manager or purchaser. Through your Team Console page on our website, you can create, delete and change the password of any "End User ID" that belongs to the "Company ID". Purchasing and assigning a license to an "End User ID" are authorities only available to a Company ID. A Company ID cannot contain any type of license on its own and therefore cannot be used to log into the software. End User ID: An "End User ID" is an account for actual users which can hold licenses and is used to log in to the software. An "End User ID" cannot be used to purchase a license through our website. An End User ID can only be used to modify some of the information on its account page (i.e. Name, Country, Territory, Region, or Profile Photo) License Purchase Team Console Access Store Item Purchase Log In To Software Company ID O O O X End User ID X X X O * Note In the case of Enterprise Users who have created their IDs before the deployment of the Company ID - End User ID structure, you would already have the Company ID designated by us. In order for you to find your Company ID, please contact us at support@marvelousdesigner.com Personal ID Guideline Personal ID: A Personal ID is an account for all personal license users. Personal ID can only purchase personal licenses. How to use My Account Dashboard In the Dashboard section, you can view the general information of your account, as well as the licenses you possess at the moment *License Users can view all licenses they have access to. They can also download different update installers under each license version in the archive list. Account On the Account section, you can check more specific information of the account, as well as modify some of the information including Name, Profile photo, Occupation, Billing Address, Country/ Territory/ Region. *Newsletter Subscription Users can either turn on and off the newsletter subscription option with this slide bar **Delete Account Users can proceed to delete their account as long as there is no active license existing at the moment License On the License section, you can check the Name of the product you have/ Expiry date of it/ Different versions of installers on Windows and Mac OS, Cancellation *Order History Users can check on your order history that includes order date, product, payment method, amount, invoice **Cancel This section shows a button for users to cancel their subscription, but for those of who have purchased a license in prepaid method or possess perpetual version will have blank in a section instead

Title: ZIPPER: Register Custom OBJ as Slider & Puller
Content: Objective Allows the user to create custom components for zippers that function dynamically in the 3D Window exactly as default provided zipper components. Location Main Menu Materials Zipper Register OBJ 3D Toolbar Zipper Tool Property Editor Shape '+' Operation Create mesh for Zipper Puller or Slider and export as an OBJ. If creating a single OBJ file for both Slider &amp Puller, the node for the Slider must be named "Slider," and the node for the Puller must be named "Puller" before export. Navigate to either of the locations listed above under "Location" and click on 'Register OBJ' or the '+' icon in the Property Editor. Select the relevant Type (Slider, Puller, Slider &amp Puller, Stopper). In the File section of the pop-up window, click on the four-square button to navigate to the location of the custom OBJ file and Double-Click to select it. Adjust the position of the Puller or Slider in the preview window. Click 'OK'. Load a garment with a Zipper. Click on the Zipper in the 3D Window. In the Property Editor for the Zipper, observe that the Slider, Puller, or Stopper the user has registered is now available to be assigned to the zipper. You can find the custom Zipper component in the dropdown menu to the right of Slider or Puller under the 'Shape' section.

Title: ANIMATION MODE: Record Animation
Content: Objective Record garment animation. Note: Follow the link Process of Making Garment Animation for your reference on creating garment animation in details. Location Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). Note: Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions. 2. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the Pause button. Copy Frame The feature is to create assets for Dynamic Wrinkle. (ver. 5.1.445) - After recording an animation of a garment and copy /paste on designated frame.

Title: Wind Controller Setting
Content: Objective Adjust and apply wind effect to create fluttering effect on garment in the 3D window. Location Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Operation Activate Wind Effect 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Environment Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Wind Toggle on (Check Box) at Activate. It is now being activated (Toggled On) and becomes in blue color. 4. Click Simulation. The Wind Effect is now being activated in the 3D window. Wind Direction Setting 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller Gizmo activates. 3. Use the Gizmo to set direction and location of the wind. 4. Click Simulation. The Wind Effect is now being activated as adjusted in the 3D window. Wind Properties Setting 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Show Wind Controller Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2. Click the Wind Controller. Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust the default values at Property Editor according to the needs. Name Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. Wind Activate Sets the activation status of the wind. Type Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. Strength Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay 0~100 Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence 0~100 Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity.

Title: Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting
Content: 1. By updating the graphics card driver, you can solve and prevent graphics card-related problems that may occur while using the Marvelous Designer software. 2. Guides you on how to properly connect your desktop graphics card and monitor. Applicable for: All users of Marvelous Designer software Common Problems 1. OpenGL version warning appears when running Marvelous Designer software as shown in the figure below. 2. Graphics/texture errors or rendering images appear strange while running Marvelous Designer software. 3. If the Marvelous Designer GPU-simulation or GPU-rendering speed is lower than the expected performance of your computer's specifications. How to Update Graphics Card Driver Step 1) Find out the product name of the graphics card (GPU) installed in your desktop computer or laptop. As shown in the figure below, you can find the model name of your graphics card (GPU) in the Performance tab of Windows Device Manager. Step 2) Search and download the latest driver matching the product name from each manufacturer's website. Note that even if the graphics card model name looks the same or similar, the drivers for laptops and desktops, and for workstations and servers are different. Search for and install the driver for the type of computer you are using. AMD Radeon Driver Download (Link) Nvidia Driver Download (Link) Intel Graphics Driver Download (Link) Step 3) Run the downloaded driver file. It is recommended to install with administrator privileges. A computer reboot may be required after driver installation. Follow the on-screen instructions. Connecting the monitor and graphics card correctly As shown in the figure below, if the monitor cable is connected to the CPU built-in GPU, the built-in GPU is mainly used instead of the external graphics card. OpenGL version warnings may occur when running Marvelous Designer in this situation. How to fix Step 1) Save the files you are working on and turn off the computer completely. Step 2) Connect the monitor cable to the external graphics card and turn on the computer. Connect all monitor cables to the external graphics card, even when using more than one monitor. Step 3) If there is no screen output on the monitor, try reconnecting the monitor power. See also Supported monitor cable types vary depending on the graphic card and monitor. If you are using the latest monitor and the latest graphic card, most support HDMI or DP (DisplayPort). Find the right cable for your monitor and graphics card. Saved search (Link) Read more Marvelous Designer software automatically detects the graphics card and driver installed in the computer when launching, and displays a warning if an unsupported graphics card or outdated driver is found. Please refer to the guide above to solve the problem. If you are using a laptop with an Nvidia graphics card, the laptop will have either an AMD processor or an Intel processor with integrated graphics GPU and Nvidia GPU, respectively, depending on the situation. If an openGL-related error appears while using the Marvelous Designer software, select 'High-performance Nvidia processor' in the Nvidia control panel as shown below and click Apply. If you set Windows Update to 'Auto', it will automatically install the latest graphics card driver. However, the driver provided by the graphics card manufacturer's website is more up-to-date than the Windows update version. It is recommended to update the graphics card driver at least once every 6 months. It helps with Marvelous Designer software as well as all other graphics programs and overall system performance and stability. To check GPU usage in Windows, select GPU in the Performance tab of Task Manager as shown below. For Windows 11 users, use a dedicated utility like GPU-z (freeware, download link) If you are using a Mac, the graphics card driver is included in macOS. If you update to the latest macOS, the latest graphics card driver is also installed. To check CPU-GPU usage on Mac, use the Activity Monitor app built-in to macOS. Also check the Marvelous Designer system requirements for graphics card-related information.
